name: Mercury removal units
applications: gas processing with aluminium cryogenic exchangers
principle: Gas passes through fixed beds of sorbent, typically metal sulfides on alumina, which react irreversibly with mercury to form stable mercury sulfide. Mercury must be removed because it corrodes aluminium cryogenic heat exchangers. Modern designs place the beds upstream, close to the wells, rather than downstream of dryers as was common historically.

process_steps.name: Downstream treating and liquefaction
equipment: acid gas removal, dehydration, cryogenic exchangers

performance.basis: Axens; matches the quantification limit of current analysers; raw gas ranges from undetected to 300 µg/Nm3

source.note: Axens blog, How to remove mercury from extracted natural gas, 14 July 2020

advantages: Simple fixed beds with no utilities
Upstream placement limits contamination of the whole plant
limitations: Upstream beds must tolerate wet, high-pressure gas
Mercury can also be carried into liquids and needs separate treatment
